Pet Rock
PET ROK
noun (Boomer slang)
Created in 1975 by Gary Dahl, a California advertising man, as a joke: an ordinary smooth stone sold in a cardboard pet carrier with straw bedding and a tongue-in-cheek manual, The Care and Training of Your Pet Rock. Priced at $3.95, it sold more than a million units in the months before Christmas 1975 and made Dahl a millionaire, then vanished almost as quickly. The phrase became shorthand for any absurd fad.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The pet rock was the great joke-fad of 1975: an ordinary stone in a box, with a manual explaining how to teach it to sit and stay. Americans bought more than a million of them. Everyone knew it was a joke; that was the joke. The Christian observation: the pet rock is the funniest commentary on idolatry ever sold at a department store. The prophets had been making the same joke for three thousand years. Isaiah describes the man who cuts down a tree, cooks his dinner over half of it, and of the rest "maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god" (Isa 44:17). Habakkuk: "Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach!" (Hab 2:19). The Psalmist on idols: "They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not" (Psa 115:5). The pet rock buyer laughed because he knew the rock could not hear. The idolater does not laugh, but his rock is just as deaf. Scripture’s answer is a different Rock entirely: "The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer" (Psa 18:2); "For their rock is not as our Rock" (Deu 32:31); "that Rock was Christ" (1Co 10:4). A grandparent can tell the story of the pet rock and ask a grandchild the question the prophets asked: what are you trusting that cannot hear you?

Webster 1828 Definition

1975 novelty (Gary Dahl): an ordinary stone sold as a pet with a training manual — the prophets’ own joke about idols (Isa 44:17; Hab 2:19), and a foil for the true Rock, which is Christ (1Co 10:4).

expand to see more

PET ROCK, n. (1975; Boomer era fad) A smooth stone marketed as a pet, sold in a carrying box with a humorous care-and-training manual; hence any absurd, short-lived fad.

Webster (1828) — PET, noun [formerly peat. Latin peto.] 1. A cade lamb; a lamb brought up by hand. 2. A fondling; any little animal fondled and indulged.

Decode for families: the pet rock was a self-aware joke; many later fads are the same joke without the self-awareness.

Key Scripture

Isa 44:17 — "And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god."

Hab 2:19 — "Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise, it shall teach! Behold, it is laid over with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it."

Psa 115:5 — "They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not:"

Deu 32:31 — "For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges."

1Co 10:4 — "And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ."

Psa 18:2 — "The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my strength, in whom I will trust; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my high tower."

Modern Corruption

A harmless joke fad that doubles as the prophets’ satire of idolatry; Scripture laughs at the deaf stone and points to the Rock that hears, which is Christ.

expand to see more

There is nothing wicked in buying a joke for $3.95. The pet rock was a parody of consumer culture, and its buyers were in on it. But it is worth noticing how easily a joke and a religion sit side by side. People who laughed at the pet rock also bought crystals for healing, wore amulets for luck, and consulted horoscopes — trusting deaf things with real hopes. The prophets would see no difference between the pet rock and the crystal except that the pet rock was honest about itself.

Scripture’s Rock is the opposite of a pet. You do not train Him; He trains you. You do not carry Him in a box; He carries you. "The LORD is my rock, and my fortress" (Psa 18:2), and Paul identifies that Rock with Christ, who followed Israel through the wilderness and gave them water (1Co 10:4). A family can keep a pet rock on the shelf as a reminder of the difference.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English pet (?)/Scots pet (a tame animal) + Old French roque (rock) → 1975 Pet Rock (Gary Dahl).

expand to see more

Pet — a tame animal kept for companionship; a lamb brought up by hand (1828)

Old French roque, Medieval Latin rocca — rock

April 1975: Gary Dahl conceives the Pet Rock; Christmas 1975: over a million sold

Hebrew tsur — rock; a title of God (Deu 32:31; Psa 18:2)

Greek petra — "that Rock was Christ" (1Co 10:4)
